correctness.rationale: Every rooted-tree function modulo constants decomposes uniquely as a sum of oriented edge-cut indicators; the edge variation is the l1 norm of cut coefficients, so the constant-preserving Markov-power operator norm equals the maximum J(P^m 1_A) over tree edge cuts. Balanced double-star automorphisms reduce this to bridge cut and leaf cut. The three difference coordinates for symmetry classes obey the explicitly given 3x3 linear matrix, with eigenmodes q=k/(k+1), -q and -1. The bridge gives exactly 1 at even m, and 1+2/(2k+1)*max(0,2k*q^m-1) at odd m, while all leaf-cut columns have TV exactly one. The strict amplification condition m<log(2k)/log(1+1/k) follows algebraically, and the scaled profile follows q^(m-tau)->e^-s for m-tau~ks. Independent rational vertex simulation of all edge-cut columns for k=1..8 and m=0..10 (880 parameter/cut-family computations) agreed with the sharp formula.
residual_risks: The precise formula is for non-lazy, unweighted, balanced double stars. Bipartite -1 mode is essential; changing laziness or branch balance changes the result. Finite checks are corroboration, not the all-size proof.

value.rationale: The balanced double star is the canonical two-community tree with a bottleneck bridge. The exact norm demonstrates a counterintuitive strict short-time increase of edge variation, parity-forced equality on every even horizon, and a sharp logarithmic-in-branch-size cutoff with a transition profile. These are precise and motivated stability phenomena for a natural Markov smoothing operator.
residual_risks: The theorem is graph-family-specific and does not imply general nonexpansivity for arbitrary trees.
